coverage_note: Six Thailand hospitality clusters with sealed corridor examples — Bangkok river, Western Gulf, Eastern Gulf, Phuket/Andaman, Krabi/Phi Phi, Samui.

partner_context.their_ambition: Centara Hotels & Resorts has a national footprint across Thailand's coastal, island, river, and gateway destinations.
partner_context.their_pressure: The signature arrival is still a diesel speedboat or congested road transfer — loud, fume-heavy, and leaking margin to third-party operators.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A premium electric water layer Centara owns end-to-end: silent arrivals, curated excursions, and predictable corridor economics on sealed geometry.

hero.title: Centara × Navier
hero.subtitle: A premium electric water layer for Thailand's coastal guest journeys
hero.what_we_do_together: Centara already sits on Thailand's best water-facing guest journeys. Navier turns those stays into a cleaner, quieter, more premium way to arrive, move, and explore — starting with six Thai clusters where the hotel footprint and destination demand overlap.

why_now: Thailand tourism is scaled and returning strongly. Centara's coastal portfolio spans river gateways, royal-coast heritage resorts, Eastern Gulf islands, Andaman arrivals, and Samui flagships — each with sealed corridor geometry ready today.

network_thesis.headline: Six clusters. One premium water layer. Centara's guest journeys, upgraded.
network_thesis.body: Centara's Thailand footprint maps cleanly to six water-rich clusters. Navier seals the corridor geometry and transparent economics; Centara owns demand, packaging, and guest service standards.

operator_model.cost: Predictable electric run cost on short, repeatable guest-paid routes.
operator_model.convenience: Fewer transfer handoffs, cleaner packaging, better timing.
operator_model.comfort: Quieter vessel, calmer boarding, premium guest experience.

proof_points.claim: Centara sits on Thailand's best water-facing destinations.
proof_points.evidence: 11 A-tier water-relevant properties in the inventory.

proof_points.claim: Corridor examples use sealed Atlas geometry.
proof_points.evidence: 7 corridors bound to route_ids on Pioneer II range.

proof_points.claim: Economics follow the hospitality operator frame.
proof_points.evidence: $1M vessel, captive guest-paid transfers, transparent run-cost skeleton.

objections.response: On diesel, weather-bound schedules, with margin leaking to third parties. Navier replaces the fleet asset with a branded electric tier Centara controls.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, and journey wallet.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $1M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total guest journey spend across transport, food, stays, experiences, and ancillary revenue the partner monetizes on-island. Journey GMV rung is in this unit.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 74% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 74% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM — matured network
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market (induced demand); we already capture ~74% — growth is demand + width, not a capture ramp

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — induced marine-transfer market
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food + stays + experiences (≈3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

phase_economics.headline: Revenue potential by phase — conservative floor first, ecosystem prize last.
phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 2 boats = $1M transport rev = 310 t CO2/yr (~$439K rev/boat).

horizons.name: Prove
horizons.vessel: N30 Pioneer II (8 pax, commercial now)

horizons.name: Scale
horizons.scope: Extend to the full mapped greenfield network
horizons.vessel: N30 Pioneer II + N35 Shuttle (12–15 pax, 2027) on dense legs

horizons.name: Mature
horizons.scope: Induced marine-transfer demand across the captive network (capture already ~max)
horizons.vessel: N35-led mix; Quanta-LR on 75–150nm regional legs (H2 2026+)
horizons.fleet_note: Pioneer-equivalent; N35 mix lowers hull count for the same throughput.

vessel_sizing.headline: Right vessel for every leg — corridor range picks the hull.

classes.role: Capillary corridors ≤ 70nm. The workhorse of Prove + Scale.
Doubles throughput per hull on dense corridors; roughly halves payback. Scale-phase workhorse.
Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

vessel_sizing.range_gate_note: ≤ 70nm → Pioneer II (now). 75–150nm → Quanta-LR (roadmap). Long legs never faked on a 70nm boat.

_render_chip_flag.confidence_display: Tag every banded rung; lead with floor + corridor COUNT (ID-traceable). Never headline the 'high' band.

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, and journey wallet.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.
